thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.ACCESSOR: Six trinkets that work while worn in a Curios slot. Discount Ring: all vis costs -3%. Stabilizer Belt: +1 knockback resistance, so the altar will not throw you around. Nutrient Talisman: every 20 ticks it sweeps your hotbar and stores food that has no potion effects (up to 100 of each kind), then feeds you when you are hungry.

Dreamcatcher: 3/4 chance to take no damage at all from tainted creatures, taint damage or tentacle damage. Tentacle Ring: when hit while standing on the ground, it summons a taintacle to fight for you. Taint Ring: wearing it makes you immune to the Taint effect and slowly restores hunger in tainted land; but wearing it outside tainted land starts withdrawal damage - and taking it off kills you outright.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.ARMORMAD: Every dyeable armor is crafted the same way: one base armor plus one Crimson Fabric, anywhere in a crafting grid (shapeless). Crimson Fabric is one white wool and two string. Once sewn, the piece has a cloth layer and any single dye will colour it. thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.ARMORSET: Six dyeable sets: Cultist Robes, Thaumium Robe, Void Robe, Fortress Armor, Praetor Armor and Knight Armor; Ranger and Archer armor additionally come in dyed and plain versions. Only the cloth takes dye - the metal and plate parts always stay original. Defense (head / chest / legs): robes, knight and ranger are 2 / 6 / 5; void robe, fortress and praetor are 3 / 7 / 6.

Fortress Armor is plate plus a surcoat: the chest gem, pauldrons and skirt plates are fixed metal pieces and only the surcoat takes dye, so the same armor looks very different in different colours. The original mod also hid or showed extra decorations based on how many pieces you wear; that part is not ported yet, so the armor always shows its plain shape - defense and dyeing still work.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.BRAINCUR: Pure Zombie Brain. It cannot be eaten or worn; it is the material for the necromancer staff rod and the other necromancy recipes in this mod.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.CAP_MECH: The Mechanist cap also multiplies vis cost by 0.95 (5% cheaper) with a craft cost of 6. Same numbers as the Sojourner cap; only the look and the name differ.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.CAP_SOJO: Caps decide how much vis each cast costs. The Sojourner cap multiplies the cost by 0.95 (5% cheaper) with a craft cost of 6 - identical to the Mechanist cap, so pick whichever looks better.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.CRYSTALA:
Crystal armour: helmet, chest and leggings -2% vis cost each, boots -1%, -7% for the whole set.
Every piece counts as runic armour and adds runic shield (8 / 24 / 16 / 8).
Defence is 2 / 3 / 2 / 1 with enchantability 25.
Its value is the discount, not the tanking.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.DYEING.1: Any single dye combined with any armor that has a cloth layer can be crafted in a grid (2x2 or larger). Only the cloth layer takes the colour; the metal, gilded and plate layers keep their original look. Dyed armor can be re-dyed as often as you like - the new colour simply overwrites the old one.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.DYEING.2: Armor with a cloth layer (names as they appear in your inventory): the Cultist set (Cultist Hood / Cultist Robe / Cultist Leggings), the Thaumium Robe set, the Bleached Void Robe set, the Enhanced Fortress set, the Praetor set, the Knight set (Cultist Helmet / Chestplate / Greaves), and the dyed Ranger and Archer pieces. Iron Fortress, Sun Knight, Husk plate, Runic armor, Crystal armor, all traveller boots and the Mask of Evil cannot be dyed.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.MERELIC_:
This chapter is a quick-reference manual for the two Middle-earth lines: the upper branch covers the 36 Forgotten Relics, the lower branch covers MiddleEarth's infused metals, wands and essentia jars.
Every branch ends with its recipe pages; those pages cycle once per second, so use JEI for a steady look.
All entries here unlock automatically - nothing has to be researched and no recipe is hidden.
[Compressed Essentia Jar] 16 vis per primal (twice a warded jar's 8).
[Double-compressed Jar] 32 vis per primal (4x).
[Starry Essentia Jar] 64 vis per primal (8x).
A jar holds all six primals at once, each with its own cap, so a full starry jar is 64 x 6 vis of storage.

Used exactly like a vanilla jar: right-click to pour the jar into your wand, sneak-right-click to store the wand's vis.
No filtering - each of the six primals has its own slot.
Careful: breaking a jar does not keep its vis - drain it before you move it.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.ME_MATER:
All ten infused ingots come from infusion: an iron ingot in the centre (gold for mithril and gilded iron) plus three thematic items on the pedestals, with aspects tuned per faction.
Ingots, nuggets and storage blocks convert both ways: 1 ingot to 9 nuggets, 9 nuggets to 1 ingot, 9 ingots to 1 storage block (decorative, saves space).
These ingots feed the Middle-earth wands and jars - stockpile them first.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.ME_SUMMO:
[Focus: Bedrock Remover] socket it into a wand and right-click bedrock: 10 aer, 10 terra, 5 ordo and 20 perditio vis removes one block. The bottom layer of the world cannot be broken.
[Warpward Ring] ring slot: -5% wand vis cost.
In the source mod the ring also suppressed warp events; the 1.21 parent has no negative-warp entry point, so that part is not wired up yet.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.ME_WANDS:
[Wand core] sets the wand's capacity: 100 vis for a faction core, 250 for a staff core. The recipe is an infusion of a silverwood rod plus three faction items - one set per faction, 23 in total.
[Faction cores] recharge five vis per primal every five seconds while in hand or inventory, but only up to 90% of capacity, so they will not keep up with sustained casting.

[Wand cap] multiplies the vis cost of every cast:/nmithril 0.65 (cheapest), galvorn and morgul 0.8, black uruk and elven steel 0.9, orc / dwarven / blue-mountain / gilded iron 0.95.
A cap costs four nuggets to craft, so make ingots first. Cap and core do not have to come from the same faction.

[Staff core] is an arcane recipe: two faction cores on the diagonal plus one thaumic charm. Assembled into a staff it holds 250 vis and takes both hands.
The other 22 factions work the same way, just swap the core; see JEI for the full list.
A staff core is still a rod, so you need a cap to finish the staff.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.RELI_BAU:
[Dark Sun Ring] ring slot: fire and lava damage heals you instead (+2), and any single hit above 12 damage is ignored entirely.
[Superposition Ring] ring slot: when two players both wear one, they occasionally swap places.
Both are pure passives that work the moment they sit in a ring slot.

[Shiny Stone] necklace slot: standing still regenerates you, faster the longer you stand.
[Deific Amulet] necklace slot: clears debuffs, puts you out when burning, and spends vis for air while underwater.
Both are quality-of-life passives, handy while fishing or idling.

[Oblivion Amulet] necklace slot: randomly applies debuffs to you. Pure collector's bait - never wear it into a boss fight.
[Ring of Discord] ring slot: no passive of its own, but with the Tome of Discord in your inventory, right-clicking the ring blinks you for free.

[Mining Charm] ring slot: +2 blocks of reach, +50% mining speed.
[Advanced Mining Charm] ring slot: +4 blocks of reach, +100% mining speed.
[Ancient Aegis] belt slot: knockback immunity and one health per second.
Their recipes follow on this branch.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.RELI_ODD:
[False Justice] works from the inventory: both the damage you deal and the damage you take are doubled.
[Chaos Core] works from the inventory: incoming damage is randomly scaled 0-2x, and you occasionally catch a random potion effect.
Both rewrite the rules while carried; together they hand your life to the dice.

[Dormant Arcanum] right-click to wake it into the 250 vis Arcanum necklace.
[Ancient Aegis] belt slot: knockback immunity and one health per second - it is a bauble, so its recipe lives on the Bauble Relics branch.
This branch only collects inventory passives and conditional triggers; everything else sits on its own branch.

[Weather Stone] right-click while it rains to clear the sky.
[Overthrower] right-click to banish the creature under your crosshair to the Nether.
The recipes for False Justice and the Chaos Core follow on this branch.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.RELI_TOM:
[Tome of Rage] fires an exploding missile.
[Crimson Spell] fires an orb that damages and weakens on hit.
[Eldritch Spell] fires a chaos orb with an area burst at the landing point.
[Ghastly Skull] fires a soul-draining bolt that heals you on hit.
All four are pure damage; their projectiles drop over distance, so aim slightly high.

[Lunar Flares] drops five flares above the targeted point.
[Tome of Primal Chaos] fires a wildly veering chaos bolt.
[Soul Tome] fires a homing projectile.
[Void Grimoire] fires a dark-matter bolt that explodes on impact.
All four care about the landing point; the chaos, soul and dark-matter shots fall under gravity, so aim high at range, and the homing one tends to hit walls indoors.

[Thunderpeal] calls lightning down at the targeted spot.
[Tome of Discord] blinks you to the targeted spot within 48 blocks.
[Dimensional Mirror] returns you to your spawn or bed for double vis.
[Apotheosis] grants absorption, regeneration and resistance.
Mobility and survival. A failed vis payment only warns you instead of wasting the cast, so charge your wand first.

[Tome of Broken Fates] works from the inventory or a curio: on death it spends 100 vis from each of the six primals to cancel the death and heal you fully, then gives either a strong buff package (75%) or a debuff package (25%), with a five-minute cooldown.
[Fated Tome] pulls the creature within 16 blocks of your crosshair to you.
[Void Drainer] right-click a vis node to drain it into your wand.
General rules: all are arcane recipes, right-click from the main hand, one-second cooldown, roughly 20 vis per cast taken evenly from the six primals of a wand in your inventory - without a wand nothing happens.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.RELI_VIS:
[Arcanum] necklace slot, stores 250 vis.
[Omega Core] necklace slot, 2500 vis.
[Oblivion Stone] necklace slot, 25000 vis.
Same usage for all three: right-click in hand to pour a wand's vis into the core, sneak-right-click to draw it back. In the necklace slot they are also recognised by Thaumcraft's charging devices and slowly fill up on their own.

[Void Drainer] right-click a vis node to drain it into your wand.
[Tome of Experience] right-click to store experience, sneak-right-click to release all of it.
The three vis cores and this tome all have their recipes on the following pages.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.RELI_WEA:
[Paradox] hit damage is random between 0 and 20, and the shortfall is dealt back to you - roll a 3 and you take 17.
[Wastelayer] same material, no extra effect; a collector's piece.
[Terror Crown] helmet slot: reveals vis nodes. While worn, hostile mobs within 24 blocks are turned on each other once a second (bosses are immune), and whatever your crosshair rests on within 32 blocks keeps suffering blindness, wither, nausea, slowness and weakness.
The crown carries 3 warp, so wearing it is never restful.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.ROD_AMBE: Amber rod: only 10 capacity, but every 5 seconds it adds 1 vis to each aspect that is not full - a wand that recharges itself while sitting in your bag.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.ROD_BREA: Bread rod: capacity 39 and no combat ability whatsoever. Its only function is to say something once in a while (one in a thousand ticks). That is the whole feature.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.ROD_NECR: Necromancer staff rod: capacity 200. It drinks aspect orbs within 3 blocks and stores them at 4.33x value - the fastest way to stock up vis, as long as there are orbs around.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.ROD_TRAN: Transmutation rod: capacity 75. It works while the wand sits in your inventory - every 4 ticks it takes whatever is above 90% of a primal aspect and gives three quarters of it to the aspects below 90%, spreading the rest back out. The result is that all six aspects stay roughly even.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.ROOT.1: This branch has no lore - it just says what each item does. Every node lists the effect, the numbers and the limits in plain language, so you can look things up quickly.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.RUNICARM: Runic armor grants a runic shield: damage hits the shield first and only reaches your health when it is empty. Charge per piece: helmet 8, chestplate 24, leggings 16, boots 8 - 56 for a full set. The shield value and its recharge are handled by Thaumcraft itself, so there is nothing to manage.

Each piece has upgrade slots: 1 for tiers I and II, 3 for tier III (Primal). A shield node upgrade adds 50% charge to that piece - 2.5x with all three slots filled on tier III. The armor also repairs its own durability, faster the more Warlord upgrades you wear.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.RUNICBOO: Runic charge on your feet: 8 runic charge plus one upgrade slot, with every traveller bonus kept - step up blocks, faster running, higher jumps and softer falls. Wear these if you want both.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.RUNICGOG: Wearing these reveals nearby aura nodes (same as the Goggles of Revealing) and cuts all of your vis costs by 5%. They also count as runic armor with 8 runic charge.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.RUNICUPG:
Runic armour upgrades at the infusion altar: I -> II -> III.
Each tier has better armour and a stronger shield.
Tier III (Primal) has three upgrade slots and looks like a full robe set.
The tier recipes follow on the next pages.

How: put any runic armour (I / II / III) in the altar centre and the items on the pedestals.
Tier I and II have one slot; III (Primal) has three.
Empty slots fill first; when full a new upgrade overwrites slot 1 - that is the only way to replace one.
Installing never wipes durability, dye or other slots. All ten recipes follow.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.SEALS.1: A blank seal, currently only a crafting ingredient. The original chest and jar seals needed a whole world-level shared inventory system (block, block entity and saved data) that this port does not have, so those items were not kept.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.TRAVELLE: All three ordinary traveller boots do the same job: step up one block automatically, run faster, jump higher and fall softer. Boots of the Explorer is the balanced one, Boots of the Wanderer runs fastest and falls softest, Runic Boots of the Traveller adds a runic shield and one upgrade slot. Numbers: step height +0.4 (a full block), speed +15% to +30%, jump +0.275 blocks, fall distance reduced by 0.25 to 0.5 per tick.

Two more are special, and both are infusion upgrades: Boots of the Explorer to Boots of the Meteor, then to Boots of the Comet. Meteor boots: jumping while sneaking launches you along your look direction and you slam the ground on landing, with a bigger explosion the longer you were airborne (1 / 2 / 3 blocks past 5 / 10 / 15 ticks), costing 1 durability per slam. Comet boots freeze the water under you as you walk (radius 5, an 11x11 area), so you can run across water.

thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.ARMORSET:
The three masks are installed by infusion as well and stay on the helmet permanently; swapping is free:/n0 Grinning Devil: mind 64 - heal 64 - armour 16, from ink sac dye + 2 iron ingots + leather + shimmerleaf + zombie brain
1 Angry Ghost: entropy 64 - death 64 - armour 16, from bone meal + 2 iron ingots + leather + poisonous potato + wither skeleton skull
2 Sipping Fiend: undead 64 - life 64 - armour 16, from red dye + 2 iron ingots + leather + ghast tear + milk bucket
While any fortress-family piece carries a mask the whole set gets an extra 0.05 in its damage-reduction factor. Infusion only sets the first mask: hold the helmet and right-click to toggle the goggles, sneak + right-click to cycle 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> none.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.MERELIC_:
[Casting relics] 13 tomes and spells, right-click from the main hand.
[Vis storage] three cores (250 / 2500 / 25000 vis) plus the tome of experience.
[Bauble relics] rings, amulets and belts - only work inside Curios slots.
[Weapons and armour] Paradox, Wastelayer, the Terror Crown.
[Oddities] the ones that work from your inventory or need a special trigger.
[Infused metals] ten ingots plus ingot / nugget / storage-block conversion.
[Middle-earth wands] cores (capacity), caps (cost), staff cores (great staves).
[Essentia jars] the three compressed tiers and the starry jar cap.
[Foci and trinkets] the bedrock remover and the warpward ring.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.ME_MATER:
[Stared Mithril] gold ingot + 9 nether stars - the expensive one, needed for the starry jar cap and the mithril cap.
[Brighten Gilded Iron] gold ingot + 3 diamonds.
[Ithildin Dwarven Steel] iron + 3 glowstone dust; [Blue-mountain Steel] iron + 3 lapis.
[Edhelmir Elven Steel] iron + 3 emeralds.
[Durnaur Orc Steel] iron + 3 blaze powder.
[Gulduril Uruk Steel] iron + 3 amethyst shards; [Black Uruk Steel] iron + 2 amethyst shards + obsidian.
[Daedelos Galvorn] iron + 3 coal; [Morgul Steel] iron + 3 blue ice.
The recipes cycle on the following pages in that order.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.ME_WANDS:
[Assembling a Middle-earth wand] In the arcane workbench: a core (or staff core) plus one cap makes a wand - the same assembly recipe Thaumcraft uses, and it costs vis.
[Why bother] Faction cores recharge themselves (five vis per primal every five seconds, up to 90%), effectively a slow charger in your pocket.
[Note] Only the six primals are refilled; anything that drinks compound aspects still needs jars or a charging pedestal.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.ME_SUMMO:
[Bedrock Remover] infusion: portable hole focus + grindstone + amber + stared mithril ingot. It is a focus, so it only works once assembled into a wand at the arcane workbench.
[Warpward Ring] infusion: mundane ring + sanity soap + 3 stared mithril nuggets.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.RUNICUPG:
1 Berserker: strength when your shield breaks, stronger the more you stack.
2 Shield Nexus: +50% shield from this piece.
3 Kinetic Feedback: an explosion when your shield breaks (no block damage).
4 Revitalizing Feedback: regeneration when your shield breaks.
5 Hardened: this piece's armour doubles after the shield breaks (Enhanced +1 only, Primal no effect).

6 Emergency Shielding: +8 shield the moment it breaks.
7 Steadfast: +20% knockback resistance.
8 Vitality: +10 max health.
9 Haste: +3% movement speed (boots only).
10 Warlord: +2 attack damage.
Stacking: 2/6/7/8/9/10 add up linearly, 3/4 scale with count, 5 counts once per piece.
tc.research_text.thaumicdyesexplor:ENCHA: Three mod-only enchantments. No enchanting table - infuse them into books.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.ENCHANTS:
All three only come from infusion; an enchanting table never offers them.
Binding: slows what you hit; at level 2 endermen, creepers and players are bound - no teleporting, and creepers cannot detonate.
Disarm: hits on non-player mobs may knock the weapon out of their hand (1/8 at level 1, 1/6 at 2, 1/4 at 3).
Night Vision: permanent night vision while worn on the head.

How: a plain book in the altar centre, the recipe items on the pedestals.
Each book has a fixed level: Binding II, Disarm III, Night Vision I.
Put the book and your weapon or helmet in an anvil - the book carries that level.

tc.research_text.thaumicdyesexplor:TE_MA: Everfull Urn, Oblivion Jar, Think Tank, Crucible of Souls and Replicator.
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.TE_MACHI:
Everfull Urn: endless water. Bucket in, water bucket out; also refills a cauldron above and douses anything burning within 4 blocks.
Oblivion Jar: essentia bin. Once wired into a tube network it destroys whatever arrives; suction 32, same as a void jar.
Think Tank: must sit on a bookshelf and holds up to 10 books. One book takes 10 seconds and the output is Thaumcraft's own Knowledge Fragment (thaumcraft:knowledge_fragment - search "Knowledge Fragment" in JEI). An enchanted book gives 1-2 fragments 67% of the time, a plain book gives one 10% of the time, and after three plain books with nothing the fourth is guaranteed. The jar puffs green particles and chimes whenever it succeeds.
Crucible of Souls: slowly drains mobs within 6 blocks; on death it yields mortuus and spiritus, extractable from any side.
Replicator: insert a sample, draw 64 praecantatio from nearby essentia sources, and it prints a copy.

[Feeding essentia through tubes] Tubes only move essentia - they neither create nor store it. Three things are needed:/n1. Source: drop items into a water-filled Crucible, then place an Arcane Alembic on top - the alembic is the source. You can also fill an Essence Phial there and pour it somewhere else by hand.
2. Pipes: run Essentia Tubes from the source to the target without gaps; a straight run auto-connects up to 15 blocks.
3. Target: it must advertise suction - a warded jar reports 32, and so does the Oblivion Jar.
Control: Essentia Valve toggles with a right-click, Directional Essentia Tube pushes one way only, Restricted Essentia Tube halves suction for short precise runs, and Filtered Essentia Tube accepts a single aspect (set it with an Essentia Filter).

In this mod the Crucible of Souls is a source (suction 0, output only from any face) and the Oblivion Jar is a sink (input only, suction 32). Crucible -> tubes -> Oblivion Jar: essentia flows on its own as mobs die.
msg.thaumicdyesexplor.think_tank.full: Jar is full (10 books) - let it burn some first
thaumicdyesexplor.research_page.TE_MACHI:
The infusion recipes for all five follow: a cauldron, a void jar, a brain in a jar, a crucible and an iron block in the centre.
Placement: the Think Tank needs a bookshelf directly underneath (plain or chiseled); otherwise right-clicking only warns you.
The Replicator must sit next to a jar or reservoir holding praecantatio, otherwise it keeps reporting it is starved.
